newsitem.title: USA: Tosco to buy Unocal 76 Products Co.
newsitem.headline: Tosco to buy Unocal 76 Products Co.

text.p: Tosco Corp said Monday that it has signed a letter of intent with Unocal Corp to buy all the operating assets of its 76 Products Co, the refining and marketing business on the West Coast which Unocal recently put up for sale.

Tosco said it will pay $1.4 billion for the assets, purchase normal inventories and assume limited environmental liabilities. In addition, Unocal will participate in future profits in the event retail market conditions and CARB gasoline premiums improve over the next seven years, up to a cumulative addition of $250 million.

Tosco is acquiring Unocal's California refining system, which has a capacity to process 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil. Also included is a retail system that currently sells over 100,000 bpd of gasoline and diesel fuel.

The retail system consists of approximately 1,350 76-branded gasoline stations, 1,100 of which are company-controlled. Tosco will acquire, as part of the purchase, the 76 brand in the refining and marketing business on a worldwide basis.

Tosco also buys a distribution system comprised of 13 company-owned oil storage terminals, three modern American-flag 40,000 deadweight-ton tankers, and 1,500 miles of crude oil and product pipeline. The purchase includes the worldwide assets of Unocal's extensive lubricants manufacturing, distribution and marketing business.

Tosco chairman and chief executive Thomas O'Malley said in a statement that the acquisition will be paid for through a combination of debt and equity. "Given the current earnings power of the Unocal assets, the equity issue should be accretive to per-share earnings," he said.

"This acquisition makes Tosco the largest independent refiner and marketer in the United States, with over 950,000 barrels per day of refining capacity and 12,000,000 gallons per day of retail fuel sales. The 76 retail system, added to Tosco's existing California properties, makes Tosco the third-largest retailer in the state of California," O'Malley added.
